title.narrative: Sri Lanka - Higher Education for the Twenty First Century Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Higher Education for the Twenty First Century Project for Sri Lanka is to enhance the capacity of the higher education system, institutions, and human resources to deliver quality higher education services in line with equitable social and economic development needs. There are four components to the project. The first component of the project is institutionalizing norms for the higher education sector. This component will develop the institutional foundation of the higher education sector in Sri Lanka through the establishment of a Sri Lanka qualification framework covering the higher education and training sectors, and the development of a quality assurance system to cover the entire higher education sector. The second component of the project is promoting relevance and quality of teaching and learning. This component will provide university development grants to improve the social and economic relevance of university education and quality and innovation grants to improve the performance of strategically selected study programs. The third component of the project is strengthening alternative higher education. This component will modernize the Sri Lanka Institute for Advanced Technological Education (SLIATE) and its network of Advanced Technological Institutes (ATIs) through curriculum and management reforms, and expand the coverage of the ATIs to under-served areas to provide more equitable access to alternative higher education. The fourth component of the project is human resource development, monitoring, evaluation, studies, coordination and communication. This component will strengthen the human resources and organizational capacity of the higher education sector, including the qualifications of academic staff of higher education institutions, and also support monitoring and evaluation, policy analyses and dissemination.

The project development objective is to enhance the capacity of the higher education system, institutions and human resources to deliver quality higher education services in line with economic and social development needs.

condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :Schedule 2. Section 1: A1. | Description :The Ministry of Higher Education shall maintain a project steeringcommittee whose composition is acceptable to the Association. | Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement :Schedule 2. Section 1: A2. | Description :The Ministry of Higher Education shall be responsible for projectimplementation with the support of the UGC and SLIATE. | Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement :Schedule 2. Section 1: A3. | Description :The Ministry of Higher Education shall maintain the Policy Planningand Development Unit with staff and terms of reference satisfactory to IDA for the coordination of national level activities. |Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement :Schedule 2. Section 1: A4. | Description :Universities shall be responsible for implementation of Part 2 of theproject: Promoting Relevance and Quality of Teaching and Learning. | Frequency :Quarterly

Finance Agreement :Schedule 2. Section 1: B1. | Description :The Ministry of Higher Education shall implement the project inaccordance with the Operations Manual and Environmental Assessment and Management Framework. | Frequency :Quarterly

Finance Agreement :Schedule 2. Section 1: B2. | Description :The Ministry of Higher Education shall prepare and implement, in amanner satisfactory to IDA, any environmental management plans required by the Environmental Management Framework. | Frequency:Quarterly

Finance Agreement :Schedule 2. Section 2: B2. | Description :The Ministry of Higher Education shall prepare and submit to IDAquarterly interim unaudited financial reports not later than 45 days after the end of each calender quarter. | Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement :Schedule 2. Section 2: B3. | Description :The Ministry of Higher Education shall submit audited financialstatements covering each fiscal year of the Recipient not later than six months after the end of such period. | Frequency :Yearly
